result:
The repository has nothing built, so I'll stage the project from outcomes instead of partitioning the requirements. Below are the spec's rulings (R1–R11) rewritten as outcomes. They are unranked and grouped into proposed tracks. I'll write no roadmap text until you rank them.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A Parquet filing-index catalog for **one real archived quarter**, with the original index bytes kept beside it | R1, R3, R6 | One quarterly `master.idx`, probably tens of MB, a handful of SEC requests. Unconfirmed (see probe below). |
| O2 | The historical baseline over a quarter range you choose, reporting each source file as complete, pending or failed | R1 | Up to about 136 quarters if the range starts at 1993 Q1. Volume is roughly O1's size times the quarter count. **The range is unset** (§4.8 has "no assumed start year"), so this can't be estimated yet. Request count is small; at 3 req/s, bytes rather than the rate limit dominate. |
| O3 | Daily indexes added on top of the baseline, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries without silent gaps | R2 | About 250 small daily files a year. Catch-up cost depends on the handoff date (`daily.start_date`, unset). |
| O4 | Re-running the parser over stored source files after a parser change, with no new SEC downloads and no duplicate filings | R6 | Local compute over O2's raw volume; the first real run measures it. |
| O5 | Readers always see a complete quarter (the last good version stays readable if a run fails), never half-written files | R9 | Storage roughly doubles per rebuilt quarter while old generations are retained. Retention policy is unset. |
| O6 | Weekly reconciliation that records later SEC corrections and holds any removal of filings until you approve that exact source file | R7, R10 | One re-read of every supported quarter per week, about O2's volume weekly. **Your time:** one approval per closed quarter that loses keys. How often that happens is unknown until it runs on real data. |
| O7 | All SEC traffic from every run shares one request budget, kept under the SEC's ceiling, so adding workers never adds SEC load | R8 | No compute cost. It caps throughput at 3 req/s (§4.8). |
| O8 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs scheduled and run on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage) | R4, R5, R11 | Azure dollars per month can't be estimated without a deployment. The first deployed run measures it. |
| O9 | Alerts, runbooks and a release record good enough to operate it: approvals, replay, rollback, SEC throttling or blocks | §4.7, §7, §8 | Mostly your time to rehearse; not material in compute. |

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A: the catalog** (O1–O7), *known progression*. The spec's §7 order already names the stages from one quarter to reconciliation. Reconciliation stays in A because it can't stand without the catalog.
- **Track B: running it on Azure** (O8, O9), *known progression*. I split this from A because a correct local catalog stands without Azure, and Azure scheduling serves a different use: unattended operation. If they were joined, the first real catalog would wait on infrastructure, identities and ADF pipelines.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), as a uv workspace with four packages.
- The spec puts all ingestion code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest/`. The other three scaffolds (`-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`) have no assigned role in the spec.
- The Azure platform (R4) comes from the ADR and spec. Both are still **Proposed**, pending acceptance.

**Roadmap name:** the spec's stem gives `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`.

**Optional probe, for the cost notes:** fetch one quarter's `full-index/<year>/QTR<n>/index.json` listing from the SEC to get real file sizes. The SEC requires an identifying User-Agent, so I'd need the name and contact email you want sent. I won't run it unless you say yes.

## One request

Please **rank the outcomes within each track, and rank Track A against Track B**. Confirm or change the two tracks and their kinds, including whether Azure belongs in its own track.
